newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bekaert says close to $95 mln Brazil deal.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bekaert says close to $95 mln Brazil deal.

text.p: Belgian steel cord and wire maker Bekaert SA said on Thursday it was close to reaching a deal with Brazil's Companhia Siderurgica Belgo Mineira (CSBM) to acquire 45 percent of CSBM's wire activities for a value of about $95 million.
As a result, a new independent company would be set up named Belgo-Mineira Bekaert Trefilarias LTDA (BMBT), Bekaert said in a statement.

Bekaert said it and CSBM had been partners for many years in three joint ventures in Brazil. These were Belgo-Mineira Bekaert Artefatos de Arame Ltda (BMB) with two production plants for steel cord in the state of Minas Gerais, and Bemaf and Cimaf in the state of Sao Paulo for steel wire and steel wire products.
The new company BMBT will operate three plants - at Contagem and Sabara in the Minas Gerais state and at Jossan in the state of Bahia. Bemaf will be integrated in BMBT.
BMBT is expected initialy to produce 400,000 tonnes of wire and wire products and to employ 1,750 people.
"This acquisition, combined with Bekaert's existing subsidiaries, reinforces Bekaert's position in Latin America," Bekaert said.

Bekaert has 61 manufacturing plants in 20 different countries. Combined sales of consolidated and associated companies was 90 billion Belgian francs in 1995, representing a sales volume of almost 1.8 million tonnes of steel wire, steel wire products and steel cord.

CSBM, with headquarters in Minas Gerais, is a business conglomerate of about 30 companies engaged in mining, production of wire rod, wire and wire products, steel cables, automotive parts and services.
It also holds participations in several industrial companies outside Brazil, and had sales revenues in 1995 of $1.2 billion.
